statusText: Mid-morning U.S. session (about two hours after cash open): the preliminary August University of Michigan consumer sentiment print has now confirmed a sharper-than-expected decline to 51.0 (vs ~54.5 consensus, down from 55.2 in July), layering on the already-absorbed July Retail Sales miss (-0.6% MoM). The combined data disappointment produced only a modest, contained cross-index reaction -- Dow and Nasdaq Composite each off roughly 0.2%, S&P 500 near flat after Thursday's record close above 7,800 -- not a confirmed persistent one-way move. NQ futures remain in the same broad range flagged in the prior run (session high near 30,232, a GEX/options-flow read near 30,264 with some timestamp uncertainty), still under the nearby ~30,300 call-wall. VIX remains calm near its 14.63 close (range 14.39-14.80); a fresher intraday VIX print was not confirmed via available sources this hour. 2Y/10Y Treasury yields (4.20%/4.68%) are unchanged from Alpha Vantage's prior read (still dated August 12, no fresher print). Oil is little changed today per fresher WebSearch reporting (WTI ~$81.24, Brent ~$87.02) after the U.S. said it can maintain its naval blockade of Iranian ports 'indefinitely' -- rhetoric reaffirming the standing Hormuz standoff rather than a new kinetic escalation. In equities, Applied Materials' beat-and-raise (fiscal Q3 revenue +25% YoY, strong AI-driven guidance) lifted semiconductor-equipment names (Lam Research, Applied Materials), a stock-specific positive that does not itself constitute index-level one-way structure. Alpha Vantage's TREASURY_YIELD, GLOBAL_QUOTE, WTI, BRENT and MARKET_STATUS calls all succeeded this run (confirming U.S. equities open) but the yield/oil/QQQ series returned the same stale prints as the prior run; TOP_GAINERS_LOSERS failed twice with transient Cloudflare gateway errors and was not pursued further. Live VIX, NQ intraday levels, the confirmed UMich actual, fresher oil pricing and equity-market context came from WebSearch.
recommendation: Current action remains EA_ON. Tail stays low because NQ itself continues to show no persistent one-way structure -- futures remain inside the same broad range flagged in the prior run, and the confirmed UMich miss plus the already-absorbed Retail Sales miss produced only a modest, contained cross-index pullback (~-0.2%) rather than a failed-pullback/repeated-extension pattern. Stress firms to the top of the moderate band because the UMich outcome, now confirmed, was a materially larger miss than consensus (51.0 vs ~54.5, down sharply from 55.2) -- a genuine surprise-magnitude driver -- even though price transmission into the Nasdaq-100 complex has remained orderly. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain active through this window regardless of the current EA_ON state. An upgrade to a higher Tail state would require an observed failed-pullback/repeated-extension reaction in NQ itself, not the confirmed data miss, the standing Hormuz rhetoric, or single-stock catalysts (e.g. Applied Materials' beat) on their own.

body: At 15:36 UTC, roughly two hours after the U.S. cash open, the preliminary University of Michigan consumer sentiment index for August has now printed and confirmed a sharper-than-expected decline: 51.0 versus a roughly 54.5 consensus estimate, down from 55.2 in July -- a larger miss than the pending scenario assessed in the prior run. This layers on July Retail Sales, which fell 0.6% MoM versus +0.1% expected (the steepest drop since May 2025) and printed earlier in the session. Despite both data points disappointing, the cross-index reaction has remained modest and contained: the Dow Jones Industrial Average and Nasdaq Composite are each off roughly 0.2%, and the S&P 500 sits near the flat line, a day after closing at a fresh record above 7,800 on Thursday's cooler inflation data. NQ futures remain within the same broad range flagged in the prior run -- an earlier session high near 30,232 and a GEX/options-flow snapshot near 30,264 (some timestamp uncertainty on this specific read) -- still comfortably under the nearby ~30,300 call-wall and above the ~30,000 put-wall; this is consistent with continued two-sided digestion rather than a confirmed persistent one-way break. VIX remains calm, last confirmed near 14.63 (range 14.39-14.80 on the most recent available read); no fresher intraday VIX print could be confirmed via available sources this hour, so this figure may understate any small real-time uptick from the data misses. Alpha Vantage's TREASURY_YIELD calls (2Y 4.20%, 10Y 4.68%, both dated August 12), GLOBAL_QUOTE (QQQ $732.07, dated August 13), WTI ($84.77) and BRENT ($93.26, both dated August 11) all succeeded this run but returned the identical stale values already published in the prior run -- no fresher daily print has posted yet on the free tier. Fresher WebSearch-sourced oil pricing shows materially different, more current levels (WTI ~$81.24, Brent ~$87.02, 'little changed' today) after the U.S. stated it can maintain its naval blockade of Iranian ports 'indefinitely' -- reaffirming the standing Strait of Hormuz standoff rather than signaling a new kinetic escalation; this reporting is treated as the more current oil read given the Alpha Vantage series has not refreshed. Alpha Vantage's MARKET_STATUS call succeeded this run and confirms U.S. equities are open; TOP_GAINERS_LOSERS failed twice with transient Cloudflare gateway errors and was not pursued further per the economical-use instruction, so breadth is inferred qualitatively from the modest, mixed index-level moves rather than a direct gainers/losers snapshot. In single-stock news, Applied Materials reported fiscal Q3 revenue up 25% YoY with strong AI-driven guidance, lifting semiconductor-equipment peers including Lam Research; Workday shares remain elevated on Silver Lake buyout talk from earlier in the week. Neither is an index-level one-way catalyst. Tail holds at 9% (low) because no persistent one-way price-path structure has been observed in the Nasdaq-100 complex itself -- NQ remains inside its established range despite two disappointing data prints, and the cross-index reaction stayed orderly and contained rather than showing failed-pullback or repeated-extension behavior. Stress firms to 44% (moderate, upper band) because the UMich outcome is now confirmed to be a materially larger negative surprise than consensus, compounding the already-absorbed Retail Sales miss -- a genuine surprise-magnitude and event-importance driver for Stress even though price transmission has remained orderly and VIX stays calm. Confidence rises modestly to 55% (medium-low) from the prior run's 52%, reflecting that the previously pending UMich print is now confirmed (removing that source of uncertainty) and MARKET_STATUS succeeded this run, partially offset by the Alpha Vantage yield/equity/oil series returning no fresher information, TOP_GAINERS_LOSERS failing twice, and continued timestamp uncertainty on the specific NQ intraday level.

lookbackSummary: Tail held in the low band (7-16%) through the trailing 24 hours as the index ground toward and then through a fresh S&P 500 record above 7,800 on soft CPI/PPI prints; Stress ran elevated to high (up to 51%) around the Wednesday/Thursday CPI-PPI and earnings window before easing into the moderate band through Friday's European morning, then firmed back into the low-to-mid 40s heading into and now through today's confirmed UMich miss and the already-absorbed Retail Sales miss, with cross-index reaction remaining contained (~-0.2%) rather than confirming broader transmission.
outlookSummary: Tail is projected to stay low (2-9%) through the next 24 hours; Stress is projected to ease from today's local high in the mid-40s as the confirmed UMich miss and Retail Sales data are fully digested through the remainder of the U.S. session, dropping into the high-teens by the ~21:00-22:00 UTC Friday close/CME weekend halt for NQ. From roughly 22:00 UTC Friday through the end of this forecast window (14:00 UTC Saturday), NQ futures are closed for the CME weekend break (reopening Sunday ~22:00 UTC), so Tail and Stress are held near a low baseline reflecting the absence of active price-path evidence and standing weekend headline/gap risk (principally the Hormuz standoff) rather than any newly observed structure. No forecast slot currently implies an action change from EA_ON. Confidence is projected to decay gradually from the mid-50s toward the low-30s as the horizon moves away from this run's evidence and, further out, away from any live trading session at all.
